item.title: Fed Needs to Implement at Least Two More Rate Increases, Dallas Fed’s Logan Says
item.content:encoded: Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases are needed given the current economic outlook.

item.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: U.S. Midterms, Jobs Data in Focus; BOE Expected to Raise Rates

item.title: French Contraction Has Slowed Eurozone Expansion, Surveys Show
item.content:encoded: Business activity in the eurozone slowed in October amid a squeeze on profit margins, a sign of fading resilience in the face of the higher energy costs.

item.title: U.S. Home-Builder Sentiment Sinks to 14-Year Low
item.content:encoded: The NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index, a gauge of builder confidence in the market for newly built single family housing, fell three points to 29 in October. That’s the lowest reading since June 2012.

item.title: America’s home-buying market is a house divided as surging mortgage rates send many buyers to the sidelines, while the affluent drive overall prices higher with big cash purchases
item.content:encoded: Surging mortgage rates are sending many buyers to the sidelines, while affluent shoppers are driving overall prices higher with big cash purchases.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Declined Slightly in October
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan survey’s headline index came in at 48, down from 48.1 in September and hovering near record-low levels.

item.title: U.K. Consumer Confidence Suffers Biggest Drop Since Pandemic
item.content:encoded: Consumer sentiment tumbled at the fastest pace since the Covid-19 pandemic this month as mounting cost-of-living pressures reversed the bounce in optimism seen over the summer.

item.content:encoded: The Iran war, tariffs and the AI build-out have pushed up the costs of materials, labor and borrowing.

item.title: U.S. Housing Starts Dropped Again in September
item.content:encoded: Housing starts fell 5.2% in September to 1.221 million. Economists had expected a reading of 1.3 million and for starts to rise 2% over the month.

item.title: PCE Inflation Accelerated Last Month
item.content:encoded: The inflation metric targeted by the Federal Reserve sped up in September, showing why elevated price increases hang over the central bank’s next moves.

item.title: Canada Retail Sales Look to Build on August’s Rebound
